html:
The Republic of the Seven Tithings was a small state in the upper Rhône valley, in what is now the Swiss canton of Valais, in the early modern period. It is on the map from 1530 to 1783, beside the Swiss Confederacy.

The seven tithings, or Zenden, were self-governing districts of the upper valley: Goms, Brig, Visp, Raron, Leuk, Sierre and Sion. They were nominally ruled by the bishop of Sion, but their assembly held more and more of the power. In 1475 they conquered the lower valley from Savoy and ruled it as a subject land. They were allies of the Swiss but not a full canton. Cardinal Matthäus Schiner, bishop of Sion, led Swiss armies in the Italian wars of the early 1500s.

The republic ended when French troops arrived in 1798 and made it part of the Helvetic Republic. After a spell under Napoleon, Valais joined Switzerland as a canton in 1815.
sum: The Republic of the Seven Tithings was a small state in the upper Rhône valley, in what is now the Swiss canton of Valais, in the early modern period. It is on the map from 1530 to 1783, beside the Swiss Confederacy.
